## What to notice in this excerpt

**Tier and independence are different questions.** Source 1 is T1 — the full transcript is in the repo and quotable. It is also INTERESTED, because the episode is vendor-sponsored. Both facts are true simultaneously. Tier measures *access*; independence measures *whose thumb is on the scale*. A registry that records only the first will present a sponsored podcast as a neutral primary source.

**Processing status governs quotability.** Source 2 says on its own face that it was "edited for clarity and length." Its words are the editor's arrangement of the speaker's — so it cannot support a verbatim quotation, no matter how primary it is. Sources 1 and 3 are uncorrected machine transcripts, which is why the case marks every correction in square brackets.

**The specific interest is named, not just the label.** "INTERESTED" alone tells a reader nothing. "Episode presented by Outshift by Cisco, an agentic-AI vendor" tells them exactly what to discount.

**Only one source is INDEPENDENT — and even that carries a caveat.** This is the finding that drives the Teaching Note's verification coda. The registry made it visible before a word of the case was written.
